message.subject: Schema 5 API and fresh-team Mod source ready for independent acceptance
message.body:
# Independent acceptance request: schema 5 and fresh-team Mod API

Recipient: CC Plugin CEO, Orca tab `c8adfae3-384d-4202-937b-e5b29d273071`, terminal `term_59c2e656-534f-4758-b1d2-e8a66a371faf`.

Herman authorized implementation and asked to be notified before passing testing to Claude. Codex has now notified him. You lead independent acceptance; do not treat this implementation report as evidence of a passing live run.

## Source and scope

Workspace: `C:/Users/Herman/Downloads/925-cc-plugins`, branch main. All work is uncommitted. Preserve all changes and the unrelated root `docs/validation/`. Do not resume or modify the original read-only provider transcript/pane. No release, push, global install/config change, reload of existing sessions, closure of retained scratch resources or migration is authorized by this handoff.

The source Mod now has an opt-in schema-5 preview. Installed clients remain unchanged. The Orca plugin still uses its native lifecycle; do not add a second engine there. Source Mod version remains 0.5.42 because this increment is unreleased; version alone therefore does not prove the new source is running.

Read `shared/team-store/SCHEMA-5.md`, `API-BOUNDARY.md`, `api.d.mts`, `api.mjs`, `src/api-domain.mjs`, `mod-native.mjs`, `mod-bridge.mjs`; Mod `hooks/shared-store.tsx`, relevant `register.tsx` changes, manifest and `types/index.d.ts`. Packaged Node files under `team-orchestrator/store/` are generated by `node team-orchestrator/scripts/sync-shared-store.mjs`; `--check` verifies byte equality.

Implemented: explicit conversation-scoped controller approval; several controllers coexist; approval survives a freshly verified resume of the same conversation/machine/project; separate current native member bindings and generations; fresh team/configuration; direct-report assignment admission; worker pickup with official role/task brief; explicit succeeded/failed outcome and evidence; separate admitting-head accepted/rejected decision. Rejected tasks block; recovery/retry is a later increment. No automatic launch/close, inbox/replay/scheduler, automatic task-window fencing, gate application or existing-team migration.

Host verification happens outside database transactions. Current approval, membership, role/configuration and binding generations are checked again under the common lease. Reconciliation and replay recheck current caller authority. Private requests accept no caller-selected actor, policy, SQL or storage configuration. Existing composer-only one-turn grants, Agent restrictions and manager write restrictions are retained for shared-bound members.

Schema 5 adds controller_approvals, member_bindings, task_briefs, assignment_attempts and task_acceptances. Schema 1–4 stores are refused without migration. Machine schema 1 is unchanged. Do not run against the prior retained schema-4 scratch DB or any real project store; use a new scratch root/database.

## Native adapter and specific risk to prove

The Mod sandbox actually refused `node:crypto` imports in a disposable runtime probe. The adapter uses packaged Node through `$.process.run` with bounded JSON stdin, no shell or persistent service. Node 22.13+ is required; the tested local Node is 26.9.0. No npm runtime dependency is needed for SQLite.

The verifier re-proves the current Orca runtime profile/epoch, exact local terminal project/context/host/incarnation, native Claude provider-session association and unique live local registry entry. A standalone read-only probe successfully verified your existing CEO session without altering it. That does NOT prove the whole Mod bridge.

**The child must also be a direct child of the matching registered Claude PID, with matching inherited ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE and ORCA_WORKTREE_ID. This runtime assumption has not had a live acceptance run. Test it first; if the real Mod uses another parent/service, report the actual process evidence and refusal. Do not weaken identity verification or hand-forge registry/ticket data to make the run pass.**

Approval is an exact panel action: it displays project/conversation, revalidates on click and mints a short-lived scoped machine-local ticket. The bridge verifies it. Model `approve:true`, an unrelated AskUserQuestion, outside-roster status and a copied conversation ID do not qualify. Do not hand-write an approval ticket for the live run. Trusted hooks/runtime/registry/local OS account/database owner remain trusted; shell/path checks are best effort, not an OS sandbox against hostile same-account code.

## Local verification already produced

- Full shared store on real SQLite + real PostgreSQL 18.6: **210 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, 49.77 s (`%TEMP%/team-api-both-final.log`). Includes 9 API tests per engine: complete flow, forged authority, concurrent controllers/resume/revocation, stale binding/member/config generations, wrong assignee/head, idempotency/reconciliation, expired pickup/failed/rejected outcomes, authority changed during lock wait, and whole-transaction rollback.
- A subsequently added real-socket native-verifier test: **1 passed**, exact conversation/incarnation, registry parent and runtime epoch (`node --test shared/team-store/test/mod-native.test.mjs`). Thus a fresh full suite should enumerate **211** tests on both engines. This socket test uses isolated native fixtures; it is not live acceptance.
- Mod suite: **365 passed, 0 failed**, 38 files (`%TEMP%/team-api-mod-tests.log`). Five new cases include actual panel-click evidence, forged model-field rejection and grant restrictions. The subprocess result is mocked in these hook unit tests.
- Mod validation passed after declaring sharedStoreStatus in PluginState; existing author/icon/license directory warnings remain. This is not a directory-submission acceptance claim.
- Orca plugin build passed; domain/bridge suite **656 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** (`%TEMP%/team-api-plugin-final.log`). Existing independent schema-4 report remains historical and unchanged.
- Packaged 16 runtime modules match source; 16 store modules passed Node syntax checks; git diff --check passed.
- Test-only preview/host harness fixes: native workspace responses now include the verified fixture project path; browser scenes use local host unless explicitly remote; the remote model-catalog case selects its remote scene. Pinned source loader handles directory index/JSON imports and the exact default RPC aggregate remains an intentionally unexecuted throwing boundary. No production native authorization check was weakened. All three pinned revisions have produced passing contract results; the oldest revision is being repeated against the final loader. Focused six browser regressions pass; the full corrected 35-case browser run is still in progress (`%TEMP%/team-api-browser-final.log`). Codex is finishing these here; you need not duplicate that work before the core/live checks.

My disposable PostgreSQL cluster is stopped after the suite. Metadata `%TEMP%/team-store-contract-pg-run.json` records the owned cluster/port and binary. If reusing it, use its exact data directory, `-o '-p <port> -h 127.0.0.1'`, role `contract_test`, database `team_store_contract_test`; no role `postgres` exists. Prefer your own disposable cluster. Do not assume the metadata port is in postgresql.conf. Keep Windows process output file-backed; you found that inherited pg_ctl pipes can outlive the launcher. Do not overlap cluster startup/shutdown commands.

## Independent acceptance to perform

1. Capture starting Git/source hashes, scratch directory and native terminal/session/registry facts before any run. Reproduce both-engine API/contract tests and useful independent denial/concurrency probes. Node 22.13 minimum is still untested here.
2. Load an isolated copy of this source Mod into NEW scratch Claude sessions only. `claude --plugin-dir` is advertised for per-session loading. Prove that the shared-store preview/tool/panel are from the new source, not the old globally installed Mod. Do not modify global installed copies/options. A test-only isolated manifest/default or session options may enable preview, but record that fixture configuration; it is not a new product default.
3. Through the actual Mod panel, approve a scratch controller and prove the real subprocess native-parent check. Prove another unapproved conversation refuses; separately approving a second retains the first. Resume the same scratch conversation on the same machine/project if feasible and re-prove its identity; no display-name inference.
4. Create one fresh team with Head and Worker through `shared_team`. Supply every setting explicitly. For two members configVersion is 5. Test fixture settings can use pickup=2 min, answer=3 min, taskWindowMinutes=null, replayIntervalMs=1000; these are fixture choices, not product defaults. Inspect current counters rather than guessing them.
5. Bind the exact native sessions with `bindMember`, target `{projectRoot,conversationId,terminalHandle,contextId}` and expected team/member/old-binding/controller generations. Inspect the current state for actual values. A restarted member incarnation needs explicit rebinding with an increased binding generation.
6. As Head, call `admitAssignment` for Worker with stable operationId, run/task/assignment IDs, full instructions/expectedResult and actor/target generations. Admission writes a durable record; no message transport is claimed. Deliver that assignment reference once through the test's existing communication method and record it separately from admission.
7. Worker calls `verifyAssignment`, reads the returned official role and brief BEFORE any fixture/file command, then performs the task and calls `reportOutcome` with explicit outcome, summary and verification evidence. Capture actual ordered primary transcript events, not parallel batches or duplicate request blobs.
8. Prove the task remains open and acceptance absent after worker outcome. Head calls `inspectAssignment`, reviews evidence, then `acceptTask` with explicit decision/reason and current generations. Prove Worker cannot accept its own work. Record the distinct attempt and acceptance rows and any refusals.
9. Retain useful scratch evidence/resources with explicit ownership; do not close existing retained sessions. Return a concrete report, defects with repros and limits to Codex via Orca. Do not declare full inbox/scheduler/gate or Orca shared-store integration accepted.

Use `/orchestration` for the report and check your mailbox at checkpoints. No live Task/Dispatch preamble exists for this ordinary terminal handoff; do not invent lifecycle IDs or emit fake worker_done. Report first confirmed defects promptly; Codex remains available to fix implementation issues.
